blocks.body:
# Congress Roster Data Quality Audit

Production-readiness assessment · July 18, 2026 Pacific

## Executive Summary

The current-member dataset passes every critical integrity check. Congress.gov advertises and returns 537 current members, and the protected production ledger contains the same 537 active bioguide IDs with no extra active records. All current members have a canonical Congress.gov source link, and the app's roster/search layer now excludes demo-only identities when the official roster is complete.

The remaining gaps are non-blocking presentation fields: 2 portraits use the explicit Capitol Ledger logo fallback, 516 official-site links depend on live profile hydration or the saved Congress.gov source URL, and 522 election dates remain hidden because Congress.gov service intervals are not verified election dates.

## Integrity Findings

The chamber totals reconcile exactly: 437 House members and 100 Senators. Read-only reconciliation also found zero extra active records and zero orphaned current-member source links. Nineteen former members remain as inactive historical records, preserving history without leaking into the current roster.

## Data Quality Gaps

No required identity, chamber, party, state, district, raw-source, or source-link field failed validation. The remaining gaps are visible and fail safely: unavailable portraits show the app logo; unavailable official links retain Congress.gov provenance; and unverified election dates display as “Not listed” instead of fabricated dates.

## Recommendations

1. Ship the roster-authority, canonical-member, bounded-fallback, and election-date corrections before enabling production reads.
2. After deployment, repeat representative, delegate, senator, search, legacy-route, and inactive-member browser QA against production.
3. Enable production database reads only after that deployment check and an explicit owner approval.
4. Treat verified election dates and direct official-site coverage as follow-up enrichment work, not launch blockers.

## Caveats

This is a point-in-time snapshot of Congress.gov and the protected production ledger. Congress.gov member detail hydration can still be unavailable during network or upstream outages; the app therefore uses a bounded current-member fallback and refuses inactive historical IDs. The audit confirms roster integrity, not editorial accuracy for every biography or future vote record.

## Further Questions

- Which verified source should own exact first-election and next-election dates?
- Should the two logo-fallback portraits be curated before launch?
- What monitoring threshold should pause production reads if Congress.gov and the ledger diverge after launch?
